_comment: Gives 'supermajority' schema_version 3 empty-tally coverage, and pins the FAILED / NOVOTES distinction from the opposite side to decision_weighted_zero_weight.json: here the tally is non-empty and the vote genuinely FAILS, so the decline guard IS satisfied by a decisive REJECT and the negative commitment is ALLOWED. On an empty tally (NoVotes) the same negative commitment would be denied. Both states deny a positive commitment, so the negative direction is the only thing that tells them apart (RFC-MACP-0007 6.2).
description: Decision Mode: 'supermajority' fails on an empty tally under schema_version 3; a genuine Failed result authorizes a negative commitment.

policy.description: Supermajority vote at threshold 0.67, initiator-only commitment, schema_version 3 fail-closed empty-tally semantics.

messages._comment: schema_version 3, zero decisive votes: NoVotes. The arm MUST fail without computing 0/0 (RFC-MACP-0012 4.1).

payload.reason: positive commitment attempted on an empty decisive tally

messages._comment: NoVotes denies BOTH directions. The decline guard requires at least one decisive explicit REJECT and none has been cast, so the negative commitment is denied too (RFC-MACP-0007 6.2). Contrast c2 below, where the tally is non-empty and the vote Fails.

payload.reason: negative commitment attempted on an empty decisive tally

messages._comment: THE FAILED / NOVOTES DISCRIMINATOR. Approve share 1/2 = 0.5 < 0.67, so the vote FAILED -- not NoVotes. Under Failed a negative commitment is allowed iff the decline guard holds, and 'agent://b' cast a decisive explicit REJECT, so it does. This is the same message shape that c1 above DENIED on an empty tally.

payload.reason: supermajority not reached; decline backed by a decisive reject
